question: Were exactly the failed proof obligations repaired, on exactly the families they failed on?

environment.preflight: PACKET_BUILD_ENVIRONMENT_READY: 13/13 passed, 0 failed, 3 not applicable (corrected; see blockerCorrection)
environment.whyItMatters: the lane preflight gates on rendering and this container cannot bind sources. Every repair here is a non-rendering repair: no ink was added and every fixture PDF is byte-identical to the committed one, recomputed from disk and recorded on its row.

blocker.what: the pinned Master Library is not present and cannot be recovered in this container
blocker.detail: scripts/rcap-corpus/bootstrap-private-corpus.sh resolves the release asset Expungement_AI_RCAP_Master_Library_Edition_1.zip from Roger-LegalEase/legalease-source-artifacts@source-corpus-2026-08-28 and the request answers HTTP 403 to this session token. verify-packet-build-environment.mjs reports PACKET_BUILD_ENVIRONMENT_NOT_READY with family_sources_bind failing, so neither --build nor --check starts for any family and no PDF can be re-rendered.
blocker.consequence: a repair that requires new ink is a rebuild, and no rebuild can run here.

environment.rasterState: BUILT_RASTER_PENDING. Nothing here is self-verified, none is RASTER_PASS, and visualDefects reads zero because nobody has looked.

blockerCorrection.supersedes: the corpus blocker recorded when these lanes were first returned

whatWasResolved.corpus: Recovered. The HTTP 403 was this session's own GitHub repository scope, not the token and not GitHub: the proxy answered "GitHub access to this repository is not enabled for this session. Use add_repo to request access." After add_repo for Roger-LegalEase/legalease-source-artifacts with access push, the release endpoint answers 200 and scripts/rcap-corpus/bootstrap-private-corpus.sh installs 51 jurisdictions / 499 files / 329 PDFs with the archive SHA-256 verified. Captain was right that it was never a permissions problem; the first FIX-A diagnosis and FIX-B's were wrong the same way.
whatWasResolved.preflight: PACKET_BUILD_ENVIRONMENT_READY: 13/13 passed, 0 failed, 3 not applicable, after rebasing onto shift base c6d7ffe7cfdf45629f873e1a0e58ae4b174d45c6 and deepening the shallow clone with a bounded git fetch --depth=1000.
whatWasResolved.corpusEnvironment: MASTER_LIBRARY_SOURCE_DIR must be exported to the Master Library install root for a build to run; the hosts require it by name and throw without it. Exporting it does not trip master_library_not_at_operational_path, which still passes. The broadcast's warning is about OFFICIAL_FORMS_SOURCE_DIR, which stays unset.

blockerCorrection.theRealBlocker: both build hosts fail before they finish. Neither is in any FIX lane's owned paths, and every FIX entry point is a three-line importer of one of them.

westHost.diagnosis: westParticipantInstructions is defined at line 1524 and its writer was never defined and is never imported. Both call sites write participant-instructions.md, so every AZ and every CA family crashes there. buildAz crashes after production-field-map.json and the census are rewritten and before any fixture is rendered, which leaves a half-rebuilt overlay if it is not restored.
westHost.alsoNeeded: the CA path calls a pikepdf bridge and fails with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pikepdf' before it reaches writeText. python3 -m pip install pikepdf fixes that; the preflight does not check for it, so a CA lane learns after it has already cleared its output directory.

eastHost.failure: AssertionError: <documentId>/canonical: finalizer reported writes that have no artifact appearance
eastHost.diagnosis: the fields it names are exactly the ones the fact allowlist binds. The finalizer reports the write, and the flattened artifact appearance streams at every measured widget carry no drawn text for it, so exactValueObserved is false. In the completeness contract's vocabulary this is an invisible write, caught by the host's own build assertion.
reproducedOn: nj_indictable_conviction-set (NJ-CN-10557/canonical; arrestOff1, guiltyDt, guiltyCrt, DefAddr2, DefBirthDt, arrest1Dt among others)

blockerCorrection.whyThisExplainsTheStaleness: commit 9a484a6 (lane S1) extended both hosts' fact allowlists and added the west host's participant-instructions writer on 2026-08-31, and no family was rebuilt afterwards. These two defects are why: the west host crashes on the new writer and the east host's new writes produce no ink. Every overlay in the fleet has been stale since that commit, and no builder lane could have rebuilt one.
blockerCorrection.consequenceForTheseRows: the rows below stay STOPPED and their reason is unchanged in substance -- a repair that needs new ink is a rebuild, and no rebuild completes. What changed is why: not a missing corpus, but two defects in hosts this lane does not own and must not edit while other lanes build from them.
blockerCorrection.whatFixANeeds: a lane that owns the two hosts. The west host needs its missing writeText helper and pikepdf in the build environment; the east host needs the finalizer to actually draw the newly allowlisted fields, or those bindings withdrawn until it can. Once either host builds, FIX-A's stopped rows are ordinary rebuilds.

noteOnOwnership: FIX07's owned paths include the nj-arrest-no-conviction overlay but not scripts/build-census-v1-nj_arrest_no_conviction-set.mjs, which is the shared east host itself and carries that family's name. The repairs here are in the overlay only; the host was read and never written.

rows.verdict: BUILT_RASTER_PENDING for the repaired obligations; seven rows returned unrepaired

obligationsRepaired.repair: the fifth family on the stale untrusted class not_supported_by_exact_participant_fact_map, which the current shared host never emits. Sixty-eight rows are the host's own required_before_filing determination on the contract's declared channel, every one disclosed by field name and page in the packet's participant-instructions.md; nine checkbox and radio terminals are elections; two are the PDF viewer buttons formPrint and formSafeClear.

obligationsStopped.whatIsMissing: a rebuild. SHARED_EXACT_FACT_ALLOWLIST["NJ-CN-10557"] binds each of these terminal names to a held fact, so a rebuild emits them as writes. They are left exactly as the stale build recorded them rather than reclassified into blanks the participant would be told to fill.
